quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas and brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is skidding. If you have anti-lock brakes, press the brakes firmly and steer straight.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: A school or school crosswalk is ahead.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on roads near schools. It warns drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Even shallow water can hide dangers. If you see flooding, turn around and take another route.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A yield sign is ahead.
A side road is entering from the left.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yield sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a yield sign is coming. Start to slow down when you see this warning sign.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill on a road with or without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This keeps your vehicle away from traffic if the brakes fail. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the vehicle rolls into the curb if the brakes fail.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot affect driving ability at recommended doses.
Medications prescribed by a doctor are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—prescription or over-the-counter—can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and reduce your driving ability. Know how your medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: When is it legal to drive in a bicycle lane?

options.text: When you need the space and the lane is empty.
When you are passing another vehicle
When parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).

questions.correctAnswerText: When parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive in a bicycle lane except when parking (where allowed), entering or leaving the road, or turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).

questions.question: When you see someone crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is far from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Wait until the person is well away from your path. Always yield the right-of-way to blind pedestrians.

questions.question: What can bad suspension cause?

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a comfortable ride. If your car bounces a lot over bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: What can happen if you abandon an animal on the highway?

options.text: You may go to jail.
You get a point against your license.
There are no legal consequences.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go to jail.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to dump or abandon an animal on the highway. You can face up to six months in jail, a fine up to $1,000, or both.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, you should yield to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived before you.
Is across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: Vehicles should go through a four-way stop in the order they arrive. If multiple vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns of possible danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and force other vehicles to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check the sides and behind your vehicle before you change lanes.

questions.question: What is the difference between a red arrow traffic light and a solid red light?

options.text: Red arrows only stop traffic that is turning.
Red arrows only control protected turn lanes.
You cannot turn on a red arrow, even if you stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn on a red arrow, even if you stop first.
questions.explanation: You may sometimes turn right on a solid red light after stopping. You can never turn left or right on a red arrow light, even after stopping.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means traffic in the lane next to the broken line may pass. Traffic in the lane next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before the turn.
When traffic on the street moves to the right.
When traffic on the street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on the street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, unless a sign forbids it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: When a cyclist is making a left turn, what can they do?

options.text: Use the left lane.
Cut through all lanes.
Wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Expect to see cyclists riding with traffic on the road. Do not be surprised if a cyclist uses the left lane when turning.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to spot possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for potential hazards. Staring only at the road directly in front is dangerous. Scan the road ahead and stay alert to vehicles around you.

questions.question: When driving on a street with multiple lanes and two-way traffic:

options.text: Drive next to other vehicles so they can see you.
Drive ahead of or behind other vehicles.
It is safest to drive in the lane next to the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive ahead of or behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Driving beside another vehicle is dangerous. The other driver may move into your lane or try to change lanes without looking. Stay ahead of or behind vehicles in other lanes instead.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol harms your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol harms your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment. Good judgment helps you react properly to things on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: To see traffic behind you:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content and its effects on your body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: What is an important step before turning?

options.text: Look at traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Slow down to turn safely.

questions.question: An orange and red triangle on a vehicle means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, road maintenance trucks, and carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: A white painted curb means:

options.text: Loading zone for cargo or passengers.
Loading zone for passengers or mail only.
Loading zone for cargo only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loading zone for passengers or mail only.
questions.explanation: At a white curb, you may stop only to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.

questions.question: Two sets of solid double yellow lines that are two or more feet apart:

options.text: Can be crossed to enter or exit a private driveway.
Cannot be crossed for any reason.
Should be treated as a separate traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be crossed for any reason.
questions.explanation: Two sets of solid double yellow lines two or more feet apart are a barrier. You cannot cross, drive on, or turn across them except at marked openings.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Consider what is happening at the intersection. If giving up the right-of-way helps avoid a crash, do it.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chances of having a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chances of having a crash.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: Slow down before entering.
Stop before entering.
Stop and wait for the green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. After you stop, you may go if it is safe, following all right-of-way rules.

questions.question: Which vehicle must always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Tank trucks marked with hazardous materials labels.
Motor homes or pickup trucks towing a boat trailer.
Any vehicle with three or more axles and weighing more than 4,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tank trucks marked with hazardous materials labels.
questions.explanation: Trucks carrying hazardous materials must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: Never make a U-turn:

options.text: in residential areas.
at or on a railroad crossing.
where there is no "No U-turn" sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: at or on a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn at or on a railroad crossing, where a No U-turn sign is posted, on a divided highway, when you cannot see 200 feet ahead in both directions, on a one-way street, in front of a fire station, or in business districts.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers to watch for people crossing the street.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Mirrors on each side eliminate blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have large blind spots. Avoid driving in these areas.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering, look left and right for vehicles or pedestrians. Look left a second time since vehicles from the left will be closer than those from the right. Check that the path through the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Stopping distance and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as speed increases.
Are not affected by speed.
Increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep hill ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.
